---- MODULE W4Od16m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Rx, Techs, NONE, MaxVer, MaxTries
ASSUME NONE \notin Rx

VARIABLES ver, hold, snap, dispensed, cver, tries

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in [Rx -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ hold \in [Techs -> Rx \cup {NONE}]
    /\ snap \in [Techs -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ dispensed \subseteq Rx
    /\ cver \in [Rx -> -1..MaxVer]
    /\ tries \in [Techs -> 0..MaxTries]

Init ==
    /\ ver = [r \in Rx |-> 0]
    /\ hold = [t \in Techs |-> NONE]
    /\ snap = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
    /\ dispensed = {}
    /\ cver = [r \in Rx |-> -1]
    /\ tries = [t \in Techs |-> 0]

Read(t, r) ==
    /\ hold[t] = NONE
    /\ r \notin dispensed
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![t] = r]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = ver[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, dispensed, cver, tries>>

Amend(r) ==
    /\ r \notin dispensed
    /\ ver[r] < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, snap, dispensed, cver, tries>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ hold[t] # NONE
    /\ LET r == hold[t] IN
        /\ snap[t] = ver[r]
        /\ r \notin dispensed
        /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {r}
        /\ cver' = [cver EXCEPT ![r] = snap[t]]
        /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, tries>>

Retry(t) ==
    /\ hold[t] # NONE
    /\ snap[t] # ver[hold[t]]
    /\ tries' = [tries EXCEPT ![t] = IF @ < MaxTries THEN @ + 1 ELSE @]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![t] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, dispensed, cver>>

Recall(r) ==
    /\ r \in dispensed
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed \ {r}
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ cver' = [cver EXCEPT ![r] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, snap, tries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs, r \in Rx : Read(t, r)
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Amend(r)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Commit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : Retry(t)
    \/ \E r \in Rx : Recall(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<ver, hold, snap, dispensed, cver, tries>>

NoStaleDispense ==
    \A r \in dispensed : cver[r] = ver[r]
====

CONSTANTS
  Rx = {rxa, rxb}
  Techs = {t1, t2}
  NONE = NONE
  MaxVer = 2
  MaxTries = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleDispense
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser lets several technicians work a shared queue of electronic prescriptions. Each prescription record carries a version number. To fill one, a technician first reads the record, taking a snapshot of its current version. While the technician works, a supervising pharmacist may amend the record, which bumps its version and invalidates any snapshot taken earlier. When the technician tries to commit the dispense, the system performs an optimistic check: it only lets the dispense through if the technician's snapshot still matches the record's live version, meaning nothing changed underneath them. A technician whose snapshot is stale is forced to abandon and retry rather than dispense against outdated instructions. A technician may be slow and hold a record for a while, but is never assumed to have failed. Dispensing is final, and once a record is dispensed it is frozen against further amendment.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every dispensed prescription was committed against the record's current version, so no stale technician ever dispenses against an outdated snapshot.

---- MODULE W4Od15m0p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Traders, NONE, MaxGen
ASSUME NONE \notin Traders

VARIABLES lock, gen, snap, trying, held

TypeOK ==
    /\ lock \in Traders \cup {NONE}
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ snap \in [Traders -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ trying \in [Traders -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ held \in [Traders -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ snap = [t \in Traders |-> 0]
    /\ trying = [t \in Traders |-> FALSE]
    /\ held = [t \in Traders |-> FALSE]

Bump == IF gen < MaxGen THEN gen + 1 ELSE gen

Read(t) ==
    /\ ~trying[t]
    /\ ~held[t]
    /\ trying' = [trying EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, gen, held>>

Acquire(t) ==
    /\ trying[t]
    /\ lock = NONE
    /\ snap[t] = gen
    /\ lock' = t
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
    /\ trying' = [trying EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ gen' = Bump
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Fail(t) ==
    /\ trying[t]
    /\ (lock # NONE \/ snap[t] # gen)
    /\ trying' = [trying EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, gen, snap, held>>

Release(t) ==
    /\ held[t]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ lock' = NONE
    /\ gen' = Bump
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, trying>>

AdminSeize(t) ==
    /\ lock # t
    /\ lock' = t
    /\ held' = [x \in Traders |-> x = t]
    /\ trying' = [trying EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE]
    /\ gen' = Bump
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Read(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Acquire(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Fail(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Release(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : AdminSeize(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<lock, gen, snap, trying, held>>

MutualExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Traders : (held[a] /\ held[b]) => a = b
====

  Traders = {ta, tb, tc}
  NONE = NONE
  MaxGen = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction whose price-cross computation is a critical resource only one trading engine may enter at a time. Engines coordinate entry through an optimistic lock guarded by a generation counter. To enter, an engine first reads the current generation, taking a snapshot. It then attempts to acquire: the acquisition succeeds only if the lock is still free and the generation still matches the snapshot it read, at which point it enters and the generation is bumped. If the lock is taken or the generation moved, the attempt fails and the engine must retry from a fresh read. An engine inside the critical section eventually releases, freeing the lock and bumping the generation again. A privileged exchange administrator may override the lock and seize the critical section for a chosen engine at any time, but the override forcibly evicts whoever was inside so that entry stays exclusive.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two trading engines are ever inside the price-cross critical section at the same time.

ASSUME Nodes = {1, 2, 3}

    /\ token \in Nodes
    /\ buf \in 0..Cap
    /\ printed \in 0..MaxJobs
    /\ pending \in [Nodes -> 0..PerNode]

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ buf = 0
    /\ printed = 0
    /\ pending = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

Succ(n) == CASE n = 1 -> 2 [] n = 2 -> 3 [] OTHER -> 1

    /\ token' = Succ(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<buf, printed, pending>>

Submit(n) ==
    /\ pending[n] < PerNode
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, buf, printed>>

Spool(n) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ pending[n] > 0
    /\ buf < Cap
    /\ buf' = buf + 1
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![n] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed>>

Print ==
    /\ buf > 0
    /\ printed < MaxJobs
    /\ buf' = buf - 1
    /\ printed' = printed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending>>

AdminFlush ==
    /\ buf > 0
    /\ buf' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, printed, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Pass(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Submit(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Spool(n)
    \/ Print
    \/ AdminFlush

  Nodes = {1, 2, 3}
  Cap = 3
  MaxJobs = 4
  PerNode = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityBounded
nl:
A print shop runs several spooler nodes arranged in a ring, coordinated by a single circulating token. Only the node currently holding the token may move a waiting job into the shared spool buffer, which serializes access to that buffer. Clients may submit jobs to any node's local queue at any time, independent of the token. When a node holds the token and has a locally queued job, it spools that job into the shared buffer, but only while the buffer has room beneath its fixed capacity. The physical printer drains the shared buffer one job at a time as it prints. The token is passed around the ring from each node to its ring successor so every node eventually gets a turn. A privileged shop administrator may flush the entire shared buffer at once to clear a jam. The shared buffer must never hold more jobs than its fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared spool buffer never contains more jobs than its fixed capacity allows.

---- MODULE W4Od0m4p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Insts, Cap, MaxVer
VARIABLES qlen, ver, log, rdver, busy

TypeOK ==
    /\ qlen \in 0..Cap
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ log \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ rdver \in [Insts -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ busy \in [Insts -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ log = 0
    /\ rdver = [i \in Insts |-> 0]
    /\ busy = [i \in Insts |-> FALSE]

Arrive ==
    /\ qlen < Cap
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log, rdver, busy>>

Take(i) ==
    /\ ~busy[i]
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ rdver' = [rdver EXCEPT ![i] = ver]
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ busy[i]
    /\ rdver[i] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ log' = log + 1
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, rdver>>

Conflict(i) ==
    /\ busy[i]
    /\ rdver[i] # ver
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, ver, log, rdver>>

Rollover ==
    /\ ver = MaxVer
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ log' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, rdver, busy>>

Next ==
    \/ Arrive
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Take(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Insts : Conflict(i)
    \/ Rollover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<qlen, ver, log, rdver, busy>>

  Insts = {ia, ib}
  Cap = 3
  MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler receives a stream of surgery requests into a bounded intake queue. When the queue is full the system applies backpressure and refuses new arrivals until space frees up. Two independent scheduler instances run against one shared pool of requests and one shared assignment record that carries a version number. An instance takes a pending request, snapshotting the record's current version as it starts work. To commit its assignment it performs a versioned write: the write is accepted only if the record's version still equals the snapshot the instance read, in which case the record version advances and the commit is logged. If the version has moved because the other instance already wrote, the instance detects the conflict and drops its stale attempt rather than clobbering the other's assignment. Periodically the record rolls over and its committed-write log resets together with its version. Because both instances share one record, the versioned write is what stops one instance's assignment from silently overwriting the other's.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of logged committed writes always equals the shared record's version, so no committed update is ever silently lost to a concurrent overwrite.

EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Students, Depts, Slots, NONE
ASSUME NONE \notin Students

Seats == Depts \X Slots

VARIABLES coarse, reg, grants, cdept, pend

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Depts -> Students \cup {NONE}]
    /\ reg \in [Seats -> Students \cup {NONE}]
    /\ grants \subseteq (Students \X Seats)
    /\ cdept \in [Students -> Depts \cup {NONE}]
    /\ pend \in [Students -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [d \in Depts |-> NONE]
    /\ reg = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ cdept = [st \in Students |-> NONE]
    /\ pend = [st \in Students |-> FALSE]

Request(st) ==
    /\ ~pend[st]
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![st] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, reg, grants, cdept>>

AcqCoarse(st, d) ==
    /\ pend[st]
    /\ cdept[st] = NONE
    /\ coarse[d] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![d] = st]
    /\ cdept' = [cdept EXCEPT ![st] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, grants, pend>>

AcqFine(st, seat) ==
    /\ cdept[st] = seat[1]
    /\ reg[seat] = NONE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![seat] = st]
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {<<st, seat>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, cdept, pend>>

Commit(st) ==
    /\ cdept[st] # NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![cdept[st]] = NONE]
    /\ cdept' = [cdept EXCEPT ![st] = NONE]
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![st] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, grants>>

Drop(st, seat) ==
    /\ <<st, seat>> \in grants
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![seat] = NONE]
    /\ grants' = grants \ {<<st, seat>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, cdept, pend>>

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students : Request(st)
    \/ \E st \in Students, d \in Depts : AcqCoarse(st, d)
    \/ \E st \in Students, seat \in Seats : AcqFine(st, seat)
    \/ \E st \in Students : Commit(st)
    \/ \E st \in Students, seat \in Seats : Drop(st, seat)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, reg, grants, cdept, pend>>

NoDoubleSeat ==
    \A st \in Students, seat \in Seats :
        (<<st, seat>> \in grants) => reg[seat] = st
====
nl:
A university course-registration system protects seat assignments with two-level hierarchical locking. To enroll, a student must first acquire a coarse lock on a department, and only then may it acquire a fine lock on an individual seat within that department. A student with a pending registration request grabs the coarse department lock if it is free, recording that it holds that department. Holding the correct department's coarse lock, the student may then claim a specific open seat: the seat's register is stamped with the student's identity and a grant record is logged. Once finished the student commits, which releases the coarse department lock so other students may enroll, while the student keeps its seat. A student may later drop a seat it holds, clearing the register and removing the grant. A student may be slow between acquiring the coarse lock and the fine lock, but is never assumed to have failed. Every seat register must agree with the outstanding grant records.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a grant record says a student holds a seat, that seat's register still names exactly that student, so no seat is ever double-allocated to two students.

---- MODULE W4Od18m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Controllers, Targets, Q
ASSUME Q \in Nat

VARIABLES stage, votes, qsz, crashed

TypeOK ==
    /\ stage \in [Targets -> {"open", "armed", "fired"}]
    /\ votes \in [Targets -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ qsz \in [Targets -> 0..Cardinality(Controllers)]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ stage = [t \in Targets |-> "open"]
    /\ votes = [t \in Targets |-> {}]
    /\ qsz = [t \in Targets |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

Vote(c, t) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ stage[t] # "fired"
    /\ c \notin votes[t]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, qsz, crashed>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, votes, qsz>>

Restart(c) ==
    /\ c \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, votes, qsz>>

Arm(t) ==
    /\ stage[t] = "open"
    /\ Cardinality(votes[t]) >= Q
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![t] = "armed"]
    /\ qsz' = [qsz EXCEPT ![t] = Cardinality(votes[t])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

Fire(t) ==
    /\ stage[t] = "armed"
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![t] = "fired"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, qsz, crashed>>

ClearVotes(t) ==
    /\ stage[t] = "open"
    /\ votes[t] # {}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, qsz, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, t \in Targets : Vote(c, t)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Restart(c)
    \/ \E t \in Targets : Arm(t)
    \/ \E t \in Targets : Fire(t)
    \/ \E t \in Targets : ClearVotes(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<stage, votes, qsz, crashed>>

FiredLegit ==
    \A t \in Targets : stage[t] = "fired" => qsz[t] >= Q
====

CONSTANTS
  Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
  Targets = {d1, d2}
  Q = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FiredLegit
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network performs an irreversible unlock-and-log operation on each door only after its controllers reach a quorum. Any controller that has not crashed may cast a vote for a given door, and a door that has not yet fired accumulates the set of controllers who voted for it. A door starts open, becomes armed once a quorum of votes is gathered, and finally fires the irreversible operation exactly once when it moves from armed to fired; the fired stage is terminal and records how large the backing quorum was at the moment it fired. Controllers may crash silently and stop voting, and a crashed controller may later restart and rejoin. Before a door fires, its accumulated votes may be cleared to start a fresh voting round. Because the irreversible operation can never be undone, it must fire at most once per door and only on the strength of a genuine quorum.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any door whose irreversible unlock-and-log has fired did so backed by at least a quorum of votes, so the one-time irreversible action never fires without genuine quorum authorization.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Feeders, Slots, NONE, Total
ASSUME Feeders = {1, 2, 3}

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES token, load, msg, delivered

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Feeders
    /\ load \in [Feeders -> 0..Total]
    /\ msg \in [Slots -> Feeders \cup {NONE}]
    /\ delivered \in 0..Total

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ load = [f \in Feeders |-> IF f = 1 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ msg = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ delivered = 0

Succ(n) == CASE n = 1 -> 2 [] n = 2 -> 3 [] OTHER -> 1

Occ == Cardinality({s \in Slots : msg[s] # NONE})

Pass(f) ==
    /\ token = f
    /\ token' = Succ(f)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, msg, delivered>>

Shed(f, g, s) ==
    /\ token = f
    /\ load[f] > 0
    /\ msg[s] = NONE
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ msg' = [msg EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, delivered>>

Redirect(s, g) ==
    /\ msg[s] # NONE
    /\ msg' = [msg EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, load, delivered>>

Deliver(s) ==
    /\ msg[s] # NONE
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![msg[s]] = @ + 1]
    /\ msg' = [msg EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ delivered' = IF delivered < Total THEN delivered + 1 ELSE delivered
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Pass(f)
    \/ \E f, g \in Feeders, s \in Slots : Shed(f, g, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, g \in Feeders : Redirect(s, g)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Deliver(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, load, msg, delivered>>

Conserved == SumOver(Feeders, load) + Occ = Total
====

  Feeders = {1, 2, 3}
  Slots = {sa, sb}
  NONE = NONE
  Total = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder redistributes a fixed total amount of electrical load across a ring of feeders, coordinated by a single circulating token. Only the feeder currently holding the token may shed load, so load-shedding is mutually exclusive. When the token holder sheds, one unit of load leaves its own feeder and enters an in-flight transfer message addressed to some other feeder. Transfer messages sit in a small pool and are delivered asynchronously: they may be delivered in any order, and while in flight a message's destination may even be redirected to a different feeder. Delivering a message removes it from the pool and adds its one unit of load to the destination feeder. The token circulates around the ring so every feeder gets a turn to shed. Load is never created or destroyed in this process: every unit is either sitting on some feeder or in flight inside exactly one transfer message.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total load summed across all feeders plus all in-flight transfer messages always equals the fixed system total, so no load is ever created or destroyed.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Lobbies, Slots, NONE, N, MaxT, K

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES pool, lobby, inflight, leaseEnd, clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..N
    /\ lobby \in [Lobbies -> 0..N]
    /\ inflight \in [Slots -> Lobbies \cup {NONE}]
    /\ leaseEnd \in [Lobbies -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT

Init ==
    /\ pool = N
    /\ lobby = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
    /\ inflight = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ leaseEnd = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

Occ == Cardinality({s \in Slots : inflight[s] # NONE})

Assign(l, s) ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ inflight[s] = NONE
    /\ clock <= leaseEnd[l]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ inflight' = [inflight EXCEPT ![s] = l]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobby, leaseEnd, clock>>

Join(s) ==
    /\ inflight[s] # NONE
    /\ lobby' = [lobby EXCEPT ![inflight[s]] = @ + 1]
    /\ inflight' = [inflight EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, leaseEnd, clock>>

Renew(l) ==
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![l] = IF clock + K <= MaxT THEN clock + K ELSE MaxT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, lobby, inflight, clock>>

Leave(l) ==
    /\ lobby[l] > 0
    /\ clock > leaseEnd[l]
    /\ lobby' = [lobby EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, leaseEnd, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxT
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, lobby, inflight, leaseEnd>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies, s \in Slots : Assign(l, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Join(s)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Renew(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Leave(l)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<pool, lobby, inflight, leaseEnd, clock>>

Conserved == pool + SumOver(Lobbies, lobby) + Occ = N
====

CONSTANTS
  Lobbies = {la, lb}
  Slots = {sa, sb}
  NONE = NONE
  N = 3
  MaxT = 2
  K = 1
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker moves a fixed population of players between a central matchmaking pool and a set of game lobbies using leases that expire over time. A lobby holds a time-bounded lease; while its lease is still valid a player may be pulled from the pool and placed into an in-flight join message addressed to that lobby. Join messages are delivered asynchronously and may arrive in any order; delivering one seats its player in the destination lobby. A lobby may renew its lease, extending its expiry relative to the current clock. When a lobby's lease has expired, a seated player leaves and returns to the matchmaking pool. A global clock advances in ticks. Throughout all of this the player population is conserved: every player is counted in exactly one place at a time, either waiting in the pool, in flight inside a join message, or seated in some lobby.

    /\ leaseEnd \in [Seats -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ posted \in [Seats -> {"no", "yes"}]
    /\ slack \in [Seats -> -MaxT..MaxT]
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxT

    /\ leaseEnd = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
    /\ posted = [s \in Seats |-> "no"]
    /\ slack = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

Grant(st, s) ==
    /\ holder[s] = NONE
    /\ posted[s] = "no"
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = st]
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![s] = IF clock + K <= MaxT THEN clock + K ELSE MaxT]

Renew(s) ==
    /\ holder[s] # NONE
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![s] = IF clock + K <= MaxT THEN clock + K ELSE MaxT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, posted, slack, clock>>

AdminGrant(st, s) ==

    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = st]
    /\ leaseEnd' = [leaseEnd EXCEPT ![s] = MaxT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, slack, clock>>

    /\ posted[s] = "no"
    /\ clock > leaseEnd[s]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseEnd, posted, slack, clock>>

    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, leaseEnd, posted, slack>>

    \/ \E s \in Seats : Renew(s)
    \/ \E st \in Students, s \in Seats : AdminGrant(st, s)
    \/ \E s \in Seats : Finalize(s)

A university course-registration system hands out temporary leases on seats and posts an irreversible transcript credit when a student finalizes enrollment. To start, a seat with no current holder is granted to a student under a lease that expires a fixed interval after the current clock. The holder may renew the lease to push its expiry forward relative to the clock. A privileged registrar may administratively grant a seat to any student with a full-length lease. ---- MODULE W4Od0m9p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Surgeries, Rooms, NONE, MaxE
ASSUME NONE \notin Surgeries

Msgs == [sur : Surgeries, room : Rooms, ep : 0..MaxE]

VARIABLES reg, epoch, pool, claims

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Rooms -> Surgeries \cup {NONE}]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ pool \subseteq Msgs
    /\ claims \subseteq (Surgeries \X Rooms)

Init ==
    /\ reg = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pool = {}
    /\ claims = {}

Submit(s, r) ==
    /\ pool' = pool \cup {[sur |-> s, room |-> r, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, epoch, claims>>

Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in pool
    /\ m.ep = epoch
    /\ reg[m.room] = NONE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![m.room] = m.sur]
    /\ claims' = claims \cup {<<m.sur, m.room>>}
    /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

DropStale(m) ==
    /\ m \in pool
    /\ m.ep # epoch
    /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, epoch, claims>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ reg' = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ claims' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

Release(r) ==
    /\ reg[r] # NONE
    /\ claims' = claims \ {<<reg[r], r>>}
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pool>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Surgeries, r \in Rooms : Submit(s, r)
    \/ \E m \in pool : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in pool : DropStale(m)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Release(r)

    \A s \in Surgeries, r \in Rooms :
        (<<s, r>> \in claims) => reg[r] = s

  Rooms = {r1, r2}

  MaxE = 2

A hospital operating-room scheduler assigns rooms to surgeries and reconfigures itself in numbered epochs. Requests to allocate a room to a surgery are issued as messages stamped with the epoch current at submission time, and these messages sit in a pool and are applied asynchronously in any order. A message is applied only if its stamped epoch still matches the system's current epoch and the target room is currently free, in which case the room's register is stamped with the surgery and a claim record is logged. Messages whose stamped epoch is stale, because a reconfiguration has since advanced the epoch, are simply discarded from the pool. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch and clears all room registers and claim records, forcing a clean reallocation. A held room may also be released, clearing its register and claim together. Because messages can be reordered and epochs advance underneath them, the register and the claim records must always agree.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a claim record says a surgery holds a room, that room's register still names exactly that surgery, so no room is ever double-allocated to two surgeries.

    /\ jobCar[j] = NONE
    /\ dpick' = [dpick EXCEPT ![d] = j]
    /\ dsnap' = [dsnap EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, jobCar, epoch>>

Commit(d, c) ==

    /\ dsnap[d] = epoch
    /\ assigned[c] = NONE
    /\ jobCar[dpick[d]] = NONE
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![c] = dpick[d]]
    /\ jobCar' = [jobCar EXCEPT ![dpick[d]] = c]

    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dpick, dsnap>>

An elevator bank is driven by two independent dispatcher instances that draw floor-service jobs from one shared pool and assign each job to a car. Assignment is reconfigured in numbered epochs. A dispatcher prepares an assignment by picking a still-unassigned job and snapshotting the current epoch. It then commits the assignment to a chosen idle car, but only if its epoch snapshot still matches the live epoch and both the car and the job are still free; committing binds the car to the job and the job to the car. If a reconfiguration advanced the epoch after the dispatcher prepared, its snapshot is stale and it aborts the preparation. A car eventually completes its job, freeing both the car and the job. A reconfiguration bumps the epoch and tears down every car-job binding so dispatch can start fresh. Because two dispatchers share one job pool, the car-to-job and job-to-car bindings must stay perfectly consistent.
SAFETY PROPERTY: a car is bound to a job if and only if that job is bound back to that car, so no car is ever double-assigned two jobs and no job is served by two cars.

    /\ inBay \in [Stations -> BOOLEAN]

A car-wash conveyor line has several loading stations arranged in a ring and one shared wash bay that is a critical resource only one car may occupy at a time. Cars arrive and queue at any station independently of the token. When a station holds the token, has a car waiting, and the bay is empty, it moves a car into the bay and marks itself as occupying it. A car in the bay eventually exits, emptying the bay. The token passes from each station to its ring successor so every station gets a turn at the bay. SAFETY PROPERTY: no two stations ever have their cars in the shared wash bay at the same time.

EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS Drones, Total, MaxE

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES tok, depot, epoch, crashed

TypeOK ==
    /\ tok \in [Drones -> 0..Total]
    /\ depot \in 0..Total
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxE
    /\ crashed \subseteq Drones

Init ==
    /\ tok = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ depot = Total
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

Deploy(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![d] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

Return(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ tok[d] > 0
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

Handoff(d, e) ==
    /\ d # e
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ e \notin crashed
    /\ tok[d] > 0
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1, ![e] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depot, epoch, crashed>>

Crash(d) ==
    /\ d \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, depot, epoch>>

Recover(d) ==
    /\ d \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, depot, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxE
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, depot, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Deploy(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Return(d)
    \/ \E d, e \in Drones : Handoff(d, e)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Crash(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Recover(d)
    \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<tok, depot, epoch, crashed>>

Conserved == SumOver(Drones, tok) + depot = Total

  MaxE = 1

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a fixed number of coverage tokens that represent responsibility for watching sectors, and it rebalances them across numbered reconfiguration epochs. Tokens start pooled at a ground depot. A drone that has not crashed may deploy, pulling one token from the depot, or return, pushing one token back to the depot. Drones may also hand off a token directly to another live drone to rebalance coverage during a reconfiguration. Any drone may crash silently and stop participating; a crashed drone keeps whatever tokens it was holding, and those tokens remain accounted for even though the drone no longer acts. A crashed drone may later recover and rejoin. Each reconfiguration bumps the epoch number. No matter how tokens are deployed, returned, handed off, or stranded on a crashed drone, the total number of coverage tokens in the system never changes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the coverage tokens summed across all drones plus those in the depot always equals the fixed system total, so coverage is never created or destroyed even when a drone crashes.

    /\ ver \in [Sectors -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ snapS \in [Drones -> Sectors \cup {NONE}]
    /\ snapV \in [Drones -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ inside \in [Drones -> Sectors \cup {NONE}]

    /\ occ = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ ver = [s \in Sectors |-> 0]
    /\ snapS = [d \in Drones |-> NONE]
    /\ snapV = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ inside = [d \in Drones |-> NONE]

Read(d, s) ==

    /\ snapS[d] = NONE
    /\ snapS' = [snapS EXCEPT ![d] = s]
    /\ snapV' = [snapV EXCEPT ![d] = ver[s]]

Enter(d) ==
    /\ snapS[d] # NONE
    /\ snapV[d] = ver[snapS[d]]
    /\ occ[snapS[d]] < Cap
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![snapS[d]] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![snapS[d]] = Bump(snapS[d])]
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![d] = snapS[d]]
    /\ snapS' = [snapS EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED snapV

    /\ snapS' = [snapS EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, snapV, inside>>

    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![inside[d]] = Bump(inside[d])]
    /\ inside' = [inside EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]

    \/ \E d \in Drones : Enter(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Retry(d)

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm limits how many drones may occupy each airspace sector, and it enforces that limit with an optimistic lock per sector. It then attempts to enter: the attempt succeeds only if the sector's version still matches the snapshot the drone took and the sector still has room beneath its capacity, in which case the occupancy rises and the version advances.   MaxVer = 3

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm maintains one shared fire-perimeter record that many drones update through a compare-and-swap protocol. To propose an update a drone snapshots the record's current version and its current value, and submits a commit request stamped with that base version and the value it computed, marking itself busy. Commit requests accumulate in a pool and are applied asynchronously and out of order. A request is applied only if its stamped base version still equals the record's live version, in which case the record takes the new value and its version advances; otherwise the request is stale, meaning another drone already committed underneath it, and it is rejected. Either way the submitting drone is freed to try again. When the version reaches its maximum the record rolls over and both value and version reset together. Because commit requests can be reordered and races are common, no committed update may ever be silently lost to a concurrent overwrite.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared record's value always equals its version count, so every accepted update is preserved and no committed update is ever silently lost.

    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(S \ {x}, f)

VARIABLES qlen, cap, total, acc, snap, busy

    /\ qlen \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ total \in 0..MaxT
    /\ acc \in [Pharm -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ snap \in [Pharm -> 0..MaxT]
    /\ busy \in [Pharm -> BOOLEAN]

    /\ qlen = 0
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ total = 0
    /\ acc = [p \in Pharm |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [p \in Pharm |-> 0]
    /\ busy = [p \in Pharm |-> FALSE]

SetCap(c) ==
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, total, acc, snap, busy>>

Arrive ==
    /\ qlen < cap
    /\ qlen' = qlen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, total, acc, snap, busy>>

Take(p) ==
    /\ ~busy[p]
    /\ qlen > 0
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = total]
    /\ qlen' = qlen - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, total, acc>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ busy[p]
    /\ snap[p] = total
    /\ total < MaxT
    /\ total' = total + 1
    /\ acc' = [acc EXCEPT ![p] = @ + 1]
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, cap, snap>>

Conflict(p) ==
    /\ busy[p]
    /\ snap[p] # total
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, cap, total, acc, snap>>

Rollover ==
    /\ total = MaxT
    /\ total' = 0
    /\ acc' = [p \in Pharm |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<qlen, cap, snap, busy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxCap : SetCap(c)
    \/ Arrive
    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Take(p)
    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Pharm : Conflict(p)
    \/ Rollover

  Pharm = {p1, p2}
  MaxCap = 2
  MaxT = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser feeds refill requests through a bounded intake queue whose capacity can be changed at runtime by a supervisor. When the queue holds as many requests as the current capacity, backpressure blocks new arrivals until space frees up or the capacity is raised. Several pharmacists draw work from the queue and each commit updates one shared dispensing-total record. A pharmacist takes a request and snapshots the record's current total as it begins. To commit, it performs a versioned write accepted only if the shared total still equals the snapshot it read, in which case the shared total advances by one and the pharmacist's own cumulative contribution advances too. If the total moved because another pharmacist already committed, the pharmacist detects the conflict and drops its stale write instead of overwriting the other's contribution. When the total reaches its maximum it rolls over and all cumulative contributions reset with it. Because capacity shifts and pharmacists race, no committed contribution may ever be silently lost.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared dispensing total always equals the sum of every pharmacist's cumulative contributions, so no committed update is ever silently lost to a concurrent overwrite.

    /\ claim[j] = NONE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = j]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![j] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pending>>

Release(j) ==
    /\ claim[j] # NONE
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![claim[j]] = NONE]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pending>>

RelCoarse(j, p) ==
    /\ coarse[p] = j
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![p] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claim, pending>>

AdminAssign(j, s) ==
    /\ reg' = [x \in Slots |-> IF x = s THEN j
                               ELSE IF x = claim[j] THEN NONE
                               ELSE reg[x]]
    /\ claim' = [k \in Jobs |-> IF k = j THEN s
                                ELSE IF k = reg[s] THEN NONE
                                ELSE claim[k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Arrive(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : AcqCoarse(j, p)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : AcqFine(j, s)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Release(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : RelCoarse(j, p)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : AdminAssign(j, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, reg, claim, pending>>

NoDoubleBin ==
    \A j \in Jobs : claim[j] # NONE => reg[claim[j]] = j
====
nl:
A print shop job spooler assigns output bin slots to print jobs using two-level hierarchical locking. An arrived job must first acquire the coarse lock on a printer, and only while holding that printer may it acquire the fine lock on an individual output bin slot on that printer; claiming a slot stamps the slot register with the job and records the job's own claim of that slot. A job may release its slot, clearing the register and its claim together, and may release a printer's coarse lock. A privileged shop administrator may forcibly assign any job to any slot, but the override strips the slot away from any previous job and strips the job away from any slot it previously held, so the register and claims stay consistent and no slot ends up assigned to two jobs. Every job's recorded claim must agree with the slot register's record of who owns it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a job claims a bin slot, that slot's register still names exactly that job, so no output bin slot is ever double-allocated to two jobs.

CONSTANTS Blocks, MaxV

VARIABLES phase, voted, val, cap

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "committing", "aborting"}
    /\ voted \subseteq Blocks
    /\ val \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxV

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ voted = {}
    /\ val = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ cap = 1

Begin ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ voted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<val, cap>>

Vote(b) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ b \notin voted
    /\ voted' = voted \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, val, cap>>

VoteNo(b) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "aborting"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, val, cap>>

Prepared ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ voted = Blocks
    /\ phase' = "committing"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, val, cap>>

DoCommit ==
    /\ phase = "committing"
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : val[b] < cap
    /\ val' = [b \in Blocks |-> val[b] + 1]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, cap>>

DoAbort ==
    /\ phase \in {"aborting", "committing"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, val, cap>>

SetCap(c) ==
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, voted, val>>

Rollover ==
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : val[b] = MaxV
    /\ val' = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, voted, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ Begin
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Vote(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : VoteNo(b)
    \/ Prepared
    \/ DoCommit
    \/ DoAbort
    \/ \E c \in 1..MaxV : SetCap(c)
    \/ Rollover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, voted, val, cap>>

NoLostUpdate == \A p, q \in Blocks : val[p] = val[q]

nl:
A subway signalling block system reserves routes across several track blocks using two-phase commit so that a reservation is applied atomically to every block or to none. A coordinator begins a transaction and moves into the voting phase. Each block votes to accept the reservation, and once every block has voted yes the transaction is prepared and moves to committing; if any block votes no the transaction moves to aborting instead. Committing applies the reservation by advancing every block's shared reservation counter together in one atomic step, while aborting leaves all counters untouched. The maximum reservation depth is a capacity that an operator may change at runtime, and a transaction may only commit while every block still has room beneath the current capacity. When every block's counter reaches the maximum the system rolls them all back to zero together. Because the update must be all-or-nothing across blocks, no block's reservation update may ever be lost relative to the others.
SAFETY PROPERTY: all track blocks always hold the same shared reservation counter value, so a two-phase-commit update is never lost on any block relative to the others.
